history.summary: SUB-SHRINE NOTE: The Ramgopalji Temple is the main pink-sandstone temple of the Galtaji complex (CSV row 2073) - the two CSV rows describe the same complex, with this row being the principal shrine. Travel literature (Wikipedia-derived text, echoed across tour sites) explicitly says 'the temple complex of Ramgopalji temple is colloquially known as Monkey temple (Galwar Bagh)' - i.e. the Ramgopalji name attaches to the whole complex in English-language travel writing, which also explains why the CSV has separate rows. The temple is dedicated to Lord Ram as Ram Gopal Ji (also described as the Sita Ram ji temple); it features pavilions with rounded roofs, carved pillars and painted walls depicting Brahma, Vishnu, Ganesha, Parvati and festival scenes, and is described as resembling a haveli. It shares the complex's 18th-century origin under Diwan Rao Kriparam. town_description: The Ramgopalji Temple is the principal temple of the Galtaji complex, set in a narrow Aravalli gorge about 10 km east of Jaipur near Khania-Balaji. It stands amid the complex's pink-sandstone pavilions, sacred kunds and large rhesus macaque population that give the whole complex its 'Monkey Temple' nickname in travel literature.
